minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee kept its project rating criteria and agreed to add a bump for engineering and design first steps.
minutes.summary: The committee met with three of five members at the start. It reviewed the capital project rating categories and agreed to keep them, adding a category for preliminary engineering or design steps. It reviewed a schedule much like last year's, discussed meeting days and recording options, and left the next meeting date and the approval of old minutes for later.

member (also deputy for the finance committee)

budget_items.what_was_said: Mandated projects carry heavy weight in the rating, and efficiency or liability reduction carries a smaller weight. Members discussed giving a similar bonus to preliminary engineering requests.

budget_items.topic: Public safety building engineering design rating
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff recalled that the engineering project was rated close to the committee's priority ratings. The member asked what bonus it would have needed.

decisions.decision: Engineering and design requests will get a modest bump in the rating, with the category named generically to cover architectural, landscape design and master planning; 10 points was favoured over 20.
Staff will build the rating categories into the budget software so projects are submitted and tallied automatically before forms go to departments.
Forms go out mid-September and are due back at the beginning of October, with department meetings in October and November and a final prioritized list by early January.
Approval of minutes for September 21 and December 6, 2021 and January 4, 2022 is placed on the next agenda.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee agreed to add a modest rating bump for preliminary engineering and design requests, favouring 10 points over 20.
The committee kept its existing capital project rating categories after reviewing them, with mandated projects weighted heavily.
Staff will build the rating categories into the budget software so projects are submitted and tallied automatically before forms go to departments.
The schedule sends forms out mid-September, due early October, with department meetings in October and November and a prioritized list by early January.
No next meeting date was set, and approval of three sets of older minutes was put on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: The rating criteria decide which departments' capital requests rise to the top of the list that later goes to town meeting voters, and the new bump makes early engineering or design work easier to rank.
The unset meeting date and unapproved minutes mean the schedule for this year's capital list is not yet firm.
